results.summary_before: This is a small square-wave tone generator that produces 16 notes across 4 octaves with an optional tremolo effect. Note and octave are selected by input pins, an enable pin gates the tone, and seven outputs drive LEDs as a simple visualizer while the audio comes from the eighth output. It requires an external RC low-pass filter, a DC blocking capacitor, and a speaker or headphones, and it is intended to be controlled from a Pi Pico or a small keyboard. The documentation is informal and notes that the project was completed under time pressure.

results.summary_before: This is an interactive 1Hz stopwatch with hardware debouncing, lap memory, alarm target, and 9600-baud UART RX/TX telemetry. It uses a 10 MHz clock and includes modules for debouncing, BCD counting, alarm comparison, and UART communication. The design is implemented in Verilog and requires external hardware such as a 7-segment display, push-buttons, DIP switches, and a USB-to-TTL serial cable for full testing. It was developed as part of the V-SPACE Demo.

results.summary_before: This design displays a bouncing Tiny Tapeout logo with an animated color gradient on a 640x480 VGA screen, with the 128x128 monochrome bitmap stored in a custom NOR ROM macro. The ROM's transistor pattern doubles as silicon art, making the logo visible in the diffusion layer of the fabricated chip. Inputs allow tiling the logo, switching to a solid color, and optionally controlling bouncing with a Gamepad Pmod. It requires a Tiny VGA Pmod and an optional Gamepad Pmod.
